- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% for 3+ consecutive days, model exhibits mean reversion bias — adjust future forecasts toward historical mean of recent 7–14 days.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods — add 1–3% upward adjustment if sentiment >0 for 5+ consecutive days.
- If true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (e.g., >15% under), check for lagged event impact — model may be reacting too early; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.
